entries.name: Morton Bruce Slater

expected.charges: Freedom Ride participation — arrested Jackson, July 8, 1961.
expected.convicted: Unresolved — the arrest is documented; the disposition is not established in the CRDL record
expected.sentence: Jailed following the July 8, 1961 Freedom Ride arrest. The CORE archive identifies Morton Slater and reproduces a fellow rider account placing him in the Parchman first-offender camp. His individual release date and total time served remain unverified.

updates.convicted: Directed verdict for the defendant on April 24, 1962 (Hinds County Court docket 12,907).

entries.name: Vernon Powell Woodward

expected.charges: Breach of the peace - Episcopal Prayer Pilgrimage at the Jackson Trailways terminal
expected.sentence: Sentenced to four months in jail and a $200 fine. Released on appeal bond September 19, 1961 after six elapsed days in custody. The later appeal was not continuous incarceration.

updates.convicted: Convicted September 15, 1961; prosecution dismissed by nolle prosequi on May 21, 1962 (Hinds County Court docket 12,939).

entries.name: Gilbert S. Avery III

expected.charges: Episcopal-clergy Freedom Ride — entered the Trailways terminal coffee shop, declined orders to leave, jailed under the Mississippi breach-of-peace statute, September 13, 1961; prosecution dismissed May 21, 1962 (Pierson v. Ray group).
expected.convicted: Yes — convicted of disorderly conduct September 15, 1961; prosecution dismissed May 21, 1962
expected.sentence: Four months in jail and a $200 fine, imposed by the Jackson Municipal Court on September 15, 1961. The prosecution was dismissed on May 21, 1962; the episode later reached the Supreme Court as Pierson v. Ray. Released on appeal bond September 19, 1961.

updates.convicted: Convicted September 15, 1961; directed verdict for the defendant on April 9, 1962.
